heading: Chap. xli.—Continuation of the same subject.
paragraphs:
Let every one of you, brethren, give thanks to God in his
own order, living in all good conscience, with becoming
gravity, and not going beyond the rule of the ministry prescribed
to him. Not in every place, brethren, are the daily
sacrifices offered, or the peace-offerings, or the sin-offerings
and the trespass-offerings, but in Jerusalem only. And even
there they are not offered in any place, but only at the altar
before the temple, that which is offered being first carefully
examined by the high priest and the ministers already mentioned.
Those, therefore, who do anything beyond that which
is agreeable to His will, are punished with death. Ye see,[175]
brethren, that the greater the knowledge that has been vouchsafed
to us, the greater also is the danger to which we are
exposed.
